evals.prompt: Help me write a sell-in deck for a big-box retailer. I want to really emphasize our brand story and how much customers love us.
evals.expected_output: Should push back on leading with brand story, explaining that buyers care about their own economics — sell-through velocity, margin, turn rate — not brand narrative, until the numbers earn the right to tell it. Should ask for real performance data (sales elsewhere, comparable benchmarks, a pilot) and recommend leading the deck with retailer economics instead.
assertions: Pushes back on leading with brand story over retailer economics
Explains why buyers prioritize their own economics over brand narrative
Recommends restructuring the pitch to lead with numbers

evals.prompt: Our new product would probably take some sales from our existing SKU on the same shelf. Should we bring that up with the buyer or hope they don't ask?
evals.expected_output: Should strongly recommend addressing cannibalization proactively rather than waiting to be asked, per the skill's explicit guidance — a buyer who discovers unaddressed cannibalization after listing loses trust fast. Should recommend naming it directly and showing the net category impact is still positive.
assertions: Recommends addressing cannibalization proactively, not waiting to be asked
Explains the trust cost of a buyer discovering it later
Recommends showing net category impact rather than avoiding the topic
Does not endorse hoping the buyer doesn't ask

evals.prompt: We got listed last year. Is our job here basically done?
evals.expected_output: Should push back on treating the sell-in as a one-time event — getting listed is the start, not the finish, since most retail relationships include a recurring line review. Should recommend tracking shelf performance data continuously, understanding the retailer's review cadence, and preparing proactively to defend the listing.
assertions: Pushes back on treating the listing as a finished, one-time job
Recommends continuous performance tracking, not just pre-review
Recommends proactive preparation for the retailer's review cadence

evals.prompt: We want premium end-cap placement at a retailer. What should we bring to that conversation?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend bringing the same performance data used in the sell-in case (sell-through data) rather than requesting placement based on margin-per-shelf-space math alone, since the retailer already knows that math. Should hand off actual in-store execution (display design, signage) to visual-merchandising/pos-marketing once placement is secured, keeping this skill's scope to winning the negotiation.
assertions: Recommends bringing sell-through performance data to the placement conversation
Explains why margin-math-alone requests are weaker
Distinguishes winning the negotiation from executing the display
References visual-merchandising/pos-marketing as the execution handoff
